item.title: India & Nine Other Nations Sign Joint Declaration To Safeguard AI Supply Chains
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: India and nine other nations have signed a joint declaration to safeguard supply chains and infrastructure that are central to…
item.content:encoded:
India and nine other nations have signed a joint declaration to safeguard supply chains and infrastructure that are central to the development and deployment of advanced AI systems. 

The agreement, called the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity, was signed on November 15 at the Pax Silica retreat, which was convened by US under-secretary of state for economic affairs Jacob Helberg.

Besides India, the declaration was also signed by representatives of the governments of the US, Australia, Israel, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the UAE and the UK.

“The declaration affirms that economic security is fundamental to national security, sets out the participants’ common understanding of the sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure that underpin super intelligence (or AI) supply chains, and declares that safeguarding them is a shared endeavor,” read a statement by the US state department.

For context, the US government refers to AI as super intelligence (SI) after President Donald Trump signed an executive order to rename it.

The declaration has termed the protection of two strategic assets – “critical” AI infrastructure and “sensitive technologies” – as a “shared endeavour” essential to the prosperity and independence of participating countries. 

The document defines sensitive technologies as goods, software, knowledge, components, inputs and means of production used in AI supply chains. The declaration noted that these technologies could provide a military advantage, create undue economic leverage and pose risks if transferred without authorisation or misused.

It also defines “critical infrastructure” as the physical and digital systems that support AI supply chains, including ports, terminals, transport, communications and logistics networks, information technology and digital platforms. The declaration adds that disruption, hostile control or unauthorised exposure of data flowing through these systems could cause significant harm.

In addition, the signatories also agreed that AI resilience would be “best” achieved through diversified and trusted supply chains and by building trusted capabilities among participants. 

The declaration also underscored the importance of coordinated efforts to address AI supply chain disruptions and non-market policies that distort the AI market. It also called for protecting private investment and ensuring a level playing field for innovation and growth.

To aid this, the declaration also proposed the setting up of working groups across five separate spaces:

  • Pro-innovation policy frameworks
  • AI adoption in key sectors
  • Supply chain cooperation across the AI stack
  • Safe harbours and supply chain security hubs
  • AI security and resilience

“We, the undersigned participants,… reaffirming (reaffirm) the importance of cooperation on the enforcement of our respective policies to protect sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure from undue access, influence, or control, as stated in the Pax Silica declaration…,” added the document. 

The San Francisco Declaration is part of the broader US-led Pax Silica initiative. The framework aims to build secure and resilient supply chains for critical minerals, semiconductors and AI infrastructure.

For India, the multilateral platform offers an avenue to coordinate with other economies on AI supply chains and critical infrastructure. This comes as India seeks to expand its domestic manufacturing in semiconductors and advanced computing, while reducing reliance on foreign sources for components and equipment.

item.title: Bombay Shaving Company’s Parent Forays Into Wellness With rE, Eyes Gym Launches
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt Ltd, the parent entity of D2C grooming startup Bombay Shaving Company, has forayed into the…
item.content:encoded:
Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt Ltd, the parent entity of D2C grooming startup Bombay Shaving Company, has forayed into the wellness category with the launch of a new brand, called rE.

Cofounded by Bombay Shaving Company chief marketing officer (CMO) Varun Gupta, the new brand sells a range of massage guns, scalp massagers, foam rollers and hot and cold packs. Its website went live on November 16.

In addition, rE also noted that it is also building a separate sub-brand called Republic. Under this, it plans to set up a network of gyms and fitness-centric brands to tap into the recovery and health category. 

Meanwhile, rE’s current product portfolio spans 14 stock-keeping units (SKUs), which will target consumers who spend long hours at desks. As per its website, products start from ₹349 for an eye mask and go all the way to ₹9,999 for a foot massager.

“… A reset that takes ten minutes and is designed with doctors, not just around them, can become a habit. We think rE can help make daily recovery as normal as brushing your teeth,” said Bombay Shaving Company founder and CEO Shantanu Deshpande.

In a statement, the startup also said that rE is pursuing partnerships with brands in areas such as fitness, sports and workplace wellness. 

“rE is pursuing partnerships across fitness, sport and workplace wellness, with a focus on bringing recovery into environments where people already train, compete and work. These include recovery zones at marathons and HYROX events, gym recovery corners and office wellness programmes,” added the new brand in a statement.

rE enters a recovery and wellness market where demand is being shaped by rising gym participation, sedentary work patterns and greater consumer spending on self-care. The brand is positioning itself around daily routines, with products intended for use after work, during commutes and before sleep.

Despite its routine-led pitch, the segment remains highly competitive. At the premium end, US-based companies like Therabody and Hyperice have built positions in percussion therapy and recovery technology. Homegrown brands like Cult, AGARO, Dr Physio and Nextup also sell massage guns, foot massagers and allied devices across lower price points.

That said, rE represents Bombay Shaving Company’s expansion beyond grooming. But its work is cut out as the brand will have to establish product credibility, distribution reach and service infrastructure against established brands.

item.title: Dreamteam Bags $53 Mn To Disrupt The CRM Space With AI
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platform Dreamteam, cofounded by former Freshworks executives, has emerged out of stealth mode. The startup…
item.content:encoded:
AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platform Dreamteam, cofounded by former Freshworks executives, has emerged out of stealth mode. The startup has now raised $53 Mn (nearly ₹498 Cr) in a strategic funding round from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest.

The startup did not elaborate how it plans to utilise the funds. 

“… CRM is among the biggest software categories ripe for disruption. I’ve worked alongside Dreamteam’s founders since day one as their vision for an AI-native CRM took shape. Their deep CRM expertise and proven record of scaling enterprise software make them uniquely positioned to lead this reinvention,” said Together Fund cofounder and partner Girish Mathrubootham.

Founded in 2025 by former Freshworks executives Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy, Dreamteam is building an AI-powered CRM platform. Its four AI agents help enterprises track commitments, flag pipeline risks and automate routine sales workflows.

The startup claims that its AI platform pulls data and context from customer conversations, emails and Zoom interactions to enable AI coworkers to automate regular work. In addition, it also allows businesses to create custom apps and dashboards using natural language without writing code.

Dreamtech claims to already cater to hundreds of companies across industries such as AI, online media, healthcare, manufacturing, and consulting. 

Going forward, Dreamteam said that it plans to focus on expanding its use cases across the entire customer lifecycle, including prospecting, onboarding and upselling. 

The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in Indian AI startups. As per Inc42 data, homegrown AI ventures raised $438 Mn across 35 deals in Q2 2026, up 265% YoY. Venture capital (VC) and private equity (PE) firms remain bullish on startups that help enterprises put AI to work across business functions.

Just last month, US-based AI code testing startup Blacksmith bagged $66 Mn in its Series C round led by Sequoia Capital. Prior to this in October itself, another enterprise AI startup AuxoAI also raised $20.7 Mn in its Series A funding round led by NTTVC.

Fractal Analytics CEO Srikanth Velamakanni also recently reportedly said that the AI analytics company is in discussions with 20-25 AI startups for potential acquisitions. 

At the heart of all this is the growing Indian enterprise AI ecosystem, which is projected to become a $71 Bn opportunity by 2030.

item.title: Oil Cools, But D2C Brands See No Way Out Of Price Hikes
item.dc:creator: Gargi Sarkar
item.description: Direct-to-consumer (D2C) startups have been facing mounting cost pressures since the US-Iran conflict drove up global crude prices, making it…
item.content:encoded:
Direct-to-consumer (D2C) startups have been facing mounting cost pressures since the US-Iran conflict drove up global crude prices, making it increasingly difficult for them to protect their already-thin margins.

Even as higher oil prices push up freight, logistics, packaging and raw material costs for new-age brands and manufacturers, revising price tags does not seem to be a viable option for them for their lack of scale and bargaining power, leaving them grappling for alternatives. 

Unlike established fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies, which can leverage bulk procurement, supplier bargaining power, and diversified portfolios to absorb cost shocks, smaller D2C brands have far fewer buffers. 

Absorbing the increase depletes their already unsure margins, while passing it on to consumers risks losing them and reacquiring them at a higher cost. It’s a catch-22 situation for them.

The pressure is particularly visible in categories such as food, beverages and personal care, for which crude-linked packaging, agricultural commodities and imported ingredients account for a significant share of procurement costs. 

Higher shipping expenses and volatility in supplier availability have added to the challenge, making it difficult for startups to plan inventory and input requirements.

The festive season did offer some respite on the demand side. Online festive sales grew 17% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹1.41 Lakh Cr in 2026, according to Datum Intelligence’s Festive Barometer. 

Elsewhere, ClickPost’s analysis of more than 80 Mn orders across nearly 400 D2C brands indicated that daily orders increased 27% YoY in the run-up to Diwali, while estimated gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 45%.

The problem is that this has not necessarily translated into an easier operating environment for D2Cs. Brands are struggling now to sustain consumer demand beyond the festive period while managing the cost of acquiring customers, fulfilling orders and replenishing inventory.

However, there’s some reason for optimism now. Brent crude, which surged to around $118 per barrel in late October, has since cooled to approximately $95 as of November 16, offering a possible reprieve to businesses grappling with rising input costs. For D2C brands, however, the relief may take time to materialise, as the impact of lower oil prices will take a while to filter through to supply chains, freight rates and packaging costs.

For D2C startups, the bigger question is no longer whether input costs will ease, but how long they will have to absorb the pressure.

How Brands Are Absorbing Cost Spikes

The bigger challenge for startups is not necessarily the rise in input costs itself, but the unpredictability of procurement prices, which makes cost planning and margin management very difficult, said the founder of a large D2C beauty brand who preferred not to be named. 

“What bothers startups most is the variation. If a supplier does not stock one product because the price has gone up, the full production (line) might stop,” he said.

For instance, a specialised ingredient may become unavailable because a supplier is unwilling to maintain inventory amid an uncertain price environment. Even if it accounts for a relatively small share of the final product’s cost, its absence can disrupt the manufacturing process altogether. “You cannot make any product with 99% ingredients. That one missing ingredient will hold the thing. Then you scramble and get it from somewhere at any cost,” the founder quoted above added. 

Brands that rely on imported ingredients or packaging materials feel the pinch harder. Shipping costs can fluctuate sharply, forcing them to choose between paying a premium to avoid production delays and waiting for freight rates to ease. Either way, higher procurement costs and the need to hold extra inventory strain working capital, leaving less money for scaling-up.

Bharat Birla, executive director at Anand Rathi Investment Banking, said rising commodity and packaging costs have squeezed larger FMCG companies too, particularly in home care, packaged foods and personal care. But for smaller brands, which lack comparable procurement scale, the impact on operating margins can be far more pronounced, he pointed out.

Food & Beverage Startups Face Most Cost Exposure

The impact of input inflation varies depending on the product category. For several non-food D2C businesses, the cost of goods sold (COGS) may account for around 15-20% of the product price, and at most 30%, according to a large D2C beauty brand founder who did not wish to be named. 

Food businesses, on the other hand, can have a significantly higher COGS, sometimes reaching 40%. This makes food and beverage brands relatively more vulnerable to fluctuations in agricultural commodities, packaging and transportation costs.

Crude oil is particularly relevant for beverage manufacturers because several packaging materials, including plastic bottles, preforms, caps and labels, are linked to petrochemical inputs.

Nikhil Doda, cofounder of Lahori Zeera, told Inc42, “Most of our raw materials depend on crude. Our preforms, caps and labels are all affected. That hit was there.” The company did not raise prices specifically to offset the recent inflation, although it implemented selective hikes in April-May 2026 as part of its regular price revision cycle, he added. 

With Reliance’s Campa expanding and Coca-Cola and PepsiCo sharpening their pricing strategies, further hikes could risk weakening its competitive position. “You cannot increase prices when Coke and Pepsi have decreased their prices from ₹20 to ₹10,” Doda said.

So, for emerging consumer brands, the pricing dilemma is sharper: with fewer buffers to absorb cost shocks, they must protect margins without pricing themselves out of the market.

Why Cutting Discounts May Be Easier Than Raising Prices

Unlike established FMCG players with decades of consumer loyalty, D2C brands rely heavily on digital advertising, promotions and discounts to acquire and retain customers, making price hikes risky in a market where consumers have plenty of alternatives. So, mid-sized and smaller companies are having to look at changes in product mix and pack sizes to manage inflation, Birla said.

The room to raise prices, however, is narrowing for all. According to Sandeep Abhange, research analyst – consumer and midcaps at LKP Securities, large FMCG companies have so far absorbed roughly half of the input cost inflation. “HUL faced 8-10% material inflation but took only 2-5% price hikes, while Dabur took 4% against 10% inflation,” he said.

Startups, Abhange said, could increasingly resort to calibrated price increases and changes in pack sizes, particularly at lower price points. Smaller packs may see grammage reductions, while larger packs could see more direct price increases.

Also, brands should evaluate input inflation alongside marketing expenditure, said the beauty brand founder. “For D2C companies, the cost of goods has a relatively limited impact on overall prices in several categories. If some ingredients become twice as expensive, the cost may go up from, say, 18% to 22%, but marketing costs around 30%.”

This means a reduction in marketing expenditure or discounting could sometimes have a greater impact on profitability than a marginal improvement in procurement costs.

Brands with healthy gross margins, repeat customers and efficient marketing strategies may therefore be better positioned to absorb inflation. Those dependent on aggressive discounts and paid customer acquisition could face greater pressure.

The challenge is particularly relevant after the festive season, when promotional activity begins to moderate and brands have to convert seasonal buyers into repeat customers.

Abhange expects another meaningful round of price increases in Q3 and Q4 FY27, particularly across categories such as detergents, soaps, biscuits, noodles and packaged snacks, which remain exposed to crude-linked inputs and agricultural commodities.

Crude Prices Have Cooled, But Will Startups See Relief?

The softening of crude prices has offered some optimism. However, even as expectations of improved global supply have weighed on prices, geopolitical and shipping-related uncertainties continue to pose risks.

For Indian startups, the transmission of lower crude prices into procurement costs is unlikely to be immediate. “Even if crude cools down, the effect on our procurement levels will take at least five to six months. It’s a process, and things should also remain stable,” Doda said. 

Suppliers may still be working with inventory procured at higher prices, while shipping and conversion costs can take additional time to adjust.

Doda added that geopolitical uncertainty makes it difficult to predict when the situation will normalise. If global prices remain stable, he expects the impact to gradually reach procurement costs over the next five to six months. 

Birla too predicts a similar timeline. This means packaging-intensive businesses may have to wait until the first half of calendar 2027 to see a meaningful reduction in some input costs, provided the decline is sustained.

The broader margin outlook, however, remains cautious. Abhange expects gross margins across FMCG companies to remain under pressure through Q3 and Q4 FY27, with stabilisation likely only from Q1 FY28 (April to June 2027) as lower crude prices and easing packaging costs gradually feed through.

The timelines are not necessarily interchangeable for every D2C business. The pace of relief will depend on the category, supplier contracts, inventory cycles and the extent to which a brand relies on crude-linked inputs.

Next Few Quarters Will Test Unit Economics

For D2C startups, the next phase will be about managing growth without allowing higher procurement and marketing expenses to erode profitability.

Lower crude prices offer a positive signal, but the relief will take time to reach procurement costs. For packaging-intensive businesses, the five-to-six-month transmission period cited by Doda and Birla suggests that meaningful cost normalisation may take until the first half of 2027, provided global prices remain stable. 

A broader recovery in FMCG margins could take longer, with Abhange pointing to Q1 FY28 as a possible turning point.

In the interim, D2Cs will have to focus on supplier diversification, inventory planning, reducing avoidable marketing expenditure and improving gross margins rather than relying solely on price increases.

The current cost cycle may not necessarily become a demand-side problem for the sector, but could reveal the difference between brands that have built resilient operating models and those whose growth depends on continuous discounts and external capital.

For emerging consumer businesses, the festive season may have brought more customers through the door, but the bigger test now is whether they can retain those customers, fulfil demand and make money from every additional order.

[Edited by Chinmay Chaudhuri]

item.title: Fractal Eyes AI Acquisitions Ahead Of Enterprise AI Scale-Up
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Fractal Analytics is evaluating acquisitions across healthcare, agentic AI and AI engineering as it looks to strengthen its capabilities ahead…
item.content:encoded:
Fractal Analytics is evaluating acquisitions across healthcare, agentic AI and AI engineering as it looks to strengthen its capabilities ahead of an expected scale-up in enterprise AI adoption.

CEO Srikanth Velamakanni told Reuters that the company is in discussions with 20-25 startups for potential acquisitions. The M&A focus would be on gaining specialised engineering talent and strengthening its relationships with large cloud computing firms and frontier AI labs, particularly in areas where Fractal wants to build deeper capabilities.

Velamakanni said the company does not have a fixed acquisition target but is open to deals worth up to ₹1,000 Cr. Its preferred acquisition size ranges between $50 Mn and $100 Mn, although there is no minimum deal value. Fractal evaluated around 800 potential acquisition targets over the past 12 months, Reuters reported.

Inc42 has reached out to the company. The story will be updated on receiving a response.

The acquisition strategy is closely tied to Fractal’s expectations of how enterprise AI adoption will evolve over the next few years. During the company’s Q2 FY27 earnings call, Velamakanni said it expects enterprise AI to scale significantly over the next year as foundation models become more capable and cheaper to run.

He pointed to improvements in models’ ability to handle complex problems and longer-horizon tasks, alongside falling inference costs. According to Velamakanni, the cost of what he termed ‘fixed intelligence’ has declined 48% quarter-on-quarter. At that rate, the cost of intelligence from a foundation model could fall 93% over a year.

He expects these changes to make large-scale AI deployment increasingly compelling for enterprises, with the impact becoming meaningful as early as FY28. Velamakanni added that this shift should also reflect in metrics such as Fractal’s revenue per employee.

Against this backdrop, the company is looking at acquisitions that can accelerate its ability to build and deploy complex enterprise AI solutions. Velamakanni said Fractal is evaluating businesses with deep AI engineering talent, strong local presence across geographies and specialised expertise in industrial verticals.

The CEO also stressed that acquisitions would not be treated merely as a growth lever. Instead, they must improve Fractal’s ‘right to win’ by materially increasing its chances of securing future business. The company is looking for deals that can create a multiplier effect on its growth potential, rather than simply adding the acquired business to its existing operations.

Velamakanni said Fractal has a healthy M&A pipeline and that its board is keen to explore the opportunity. He added that the company has sufficient cash to pursue deals and expects to announce more transactions soon.

Earlier in November, Fractal acquired Geneva-based analytics firm PricingOne through its subsidiary Asper for 1.32 Mn Swiss francs ($1.57 Mn). Velamakanni described the transaction as an acqui-hire, which would also give Asper.ai a foothold in Europe.

The acquisition push comes as Fractal sharpens its focus on enterprise AI following an overhaul of its operating model. In April, the company reorganised its business around three pillars: AI-led Transformation, AI Foundations, and AI Work & Workforce.

The structure is intended to strengthen its enterprise AI offerings, build capabilities around agentic AI governance and responsible AI, and help businesses redesign workflows and workforce capabilities for AI adoption. Its agentic AI platform, Cogentiq, is positioned as the common technology layer across the three divisions.

As part of the restructuring, Fractal announced a leadership reshuffle in May, appointing Kunal Jain as head of AI workforce transformation and Suraj Amonkar as chief AI research officer. Matthew Gennone was given additional responsibility as chief commercial officer and CEO of Cogentiq.

Fractal Analytics Q2 FY27

Fractal reported record revenue from operations of ₹956.5 Cr in Q2 FY27, up nearly 20% from ₹798.5 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Revenue also grew 4.8% sequentially from ₹912.5 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Its net profit more than doubled 139% YoY to ₹79.2 Cr, compared with ₹33.2 Cr in Q2 FY26. However, profit declined sequentially from ₹115.8 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 30% YoY to ₹154.9 Cr during the quarter, while the adjusted EBITDA margin improved 123 basis points to 16.2%. The company attributed the improvement to operating leverage, while noting that investments in AI engineering talent had a short-term impact on gross margins.

Among its business verticals, healthcare and life sciences (HLS) recorded the highest revenue growth of 79% YoY in Q2 FY27. Revenue from banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) grew 30%, while consumer packaged goods and retail (CPGR), its largest vertical, reported 19% growth. Revenue from telecom, media and technology (TMT) clients, however, declined 18% during the quarter.

Fractal attributed its performance to rising revenues, improving margins, increased client spending and growth across key verticals.

Founded in 2000, Fractal provides AI and advanced analytics solutions to enterprises, including Google, Citibank, Nestlé and Wells Fargo. It also earns revenue through licensing and subscriptions for its AI platforms, including Cogentiq, Iqigai and Kalaido.ai.

The company made its stock market debut earlier this year, listing at ₹876 on the NSE, a 2.7% discount to its IPO price of ₹900. On the BSE, its shares listed at the issue price of ₹900.

Shares of Fractal ended today’s trading session 3.41% lower at ₹802.80 apiece on the BSE/

item.title: CERT-In Flags Fresh Vulnerabilities In eMudhra’s emBridge Tool
item.dc:creator: Shraddha Goled
item.description: CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) has now flagged new security flaws in eMudhra’s digital signature utility unit, emBridge, weeks…
item.content:encoded:
CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) has now flagged new security flaws in eMudhra’s digital signature utility unit, emBridge, weeks after the cybersecurity firm faced a major cybersecurity incident. 

On November 13, the national nodal agency for cyber security incident response, issued a vulnerability note on emBridge, highlighting that the software could potentially allow unauthorised entities on the same local area network (LAN) to access files and directory names on an impacted device. 

The agency classified this threat as a ‘low-severity’ cybersecurity flaw.  The issue came into picture after cybersecurity expert Karan Saini reported the vulnerability to CERT-In. 

What Is the emBridge Flaw?

Web browsers cannot talk directly to the USB tokens that hold a user’s digital signature certificate (DSC). emBridge bridges that gap. It is a client-side application that allows web portals to communicate with DSC and hardware tokens installed on a user’s computer. 

According to CERT-In, a set of file-browsing functions inside this interface did not check whether the request came from an authorised source. These functions run with the highest system privileges on Windows. An attacker on the same local network could use a malicious webpage to send requests to emBridge and map out the file and folder names on the targeted machine.

The affected versions are 5.9.1.x to 5.9.3.x on Windows, 3.2.4.x to 3.2.6.x on macOS, and 3.2.0.x to 3.3.0.x on Ubuntu and Red Hat Linux. CERT-In asked users to upgrade to version 5.9.4.x or later on Windows, 3.2.7.x or later on macOS, and 3.3.1.x or later on Linux.

Several government portals rely on emBridge for DSC-based signing, including the Ministry of Corporate Affairs’ MCA V3 portal, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and the National Single Window System. The Income Tax Department also recommends it for managing DSCs. 

However, the agency said that the flaw does not give access to the contents of files, does not allow files to be changed or deleted, does not allow code to run, and does not expose cryptographic keys or token PINs. 

eMudhra published its own advisory on the CVE and said it fixed the issue on November 11, two days before CERT-In’s note, by removing the file-browsing functions from emBridge altogether. “With these endpoints removed, the file enumeration capability is no longer available through emBridge,” the company said.

eMudhra rated the flaw’s impact and risk as low. According to its advisory, an attacker could at most see the names of drives, files and folders on a user’s computer. File contents, cryptographic keys, token PINs, and signing operations were not exposed. 

An attack would also need several conditions at once: an affected emBridge version, a malicious webpage hosted on the same local network, the user opening it, and a browser without Local Network Access restrictions. The company added that its firewall and local-only request handling block direct access from other machines.

Expert Saini, who had first uncovered the vulnerabilities, posted on X that while the bug was trivial, eMudhra’s own advisory has further downplayed it.

eMudhra in its statement to Inc42 said that every digital signature certificate needs the user to enter the token PIN before it can be used, and pointed out that CERT-In’s note confirmed keys and token PINs had not been exposed.

“Identifying and fixing vulnerabilities is a routine part of responsible software development,” a company spokesperson said, adding that large global vendors like Microsoft, Oracle, Google, and Adobe addressed thousands of vulnerabilities every month. 

The October Incident

On October 17, a security researcher reported that the private keys behind eight of eMudhra’s intermediate certificate authority certificates had been generated so weakly that they could be worked out from public data in under a second. eMudhra revoked the certificates on October 18, and browser makers moved to block them and distrust the root they chained to.

The company traced the weak keys to a script error during an April 2025 key-generation ceremony.

The fallout was swift. eMudhra said it would exit the global SSL/TLS certificate business, its shares fell sharply over two days, the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) set up a special team to probe the incident, and on October 30 the company appointed KPMG as an independent reviewer of the incident and its security controls.

item.title: Karnataka Halts Green SM Taxi Licensing To Protect Local Interest
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: The Karnataka government has reportedly halted the registration of new taxis operated by Vingroup-backed Green SM days after clearing its…
item.content:encoded:
The Karnataka government has reportedly halted the registration of new taxis operated by Vingroup-backed Green SM days after clearing its operation within the state. Alongside this, the transport department is said to be planning to make fare meters compulsory for all cabs, including those operating through ride-hailing platforms such as Ola and Uber.

Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh cited the need to protect the interests of local taxi owners and drivers as an explanation for the ban, as per a report by Moneycontrol. 

The state government has directed transport department officials to stop registering new Green SM taxis until further orders, even as around 100 vehicles operated by the company have already been registered to ply on Karnataka roads. 

That said, the state government is yet to take a final call on whether Green SM will be allowed to continue its operations in Karnataka.

Questions sent to Green SM remained unanswered at the time of publication. The story will be updated upon receiving a response. 

The latest action follows protests by Bengaluru-based private transport associations such as Karnataka Rajya Chalakara Parishath and Peace Auto Union.

The e-taxi operator, part of Vietnam’s Vingroup, which also operates electric car OEM Vinfast, received an aggregator licence from the Karnataka Transport Department in November 2026, valid until September 2031.

Protesting associations have questioned the licensing process and alleged that Green SM’s vehicles were registered without meeting mandatory requirements, including digital fare meters, taxi display boards, GPS equipment and driver documentation.

They have also raised concerns about the impact of another large fleet operator on the earnings of existing taxi drivers, particularly those who have taken loans to purchase their vehicles, seeking an examination of the permissions granted to the company and the potential impact on local operators from the Karnataka Governor. 

Taxi and auto unions in the state have a long track record of opposing ride-hailing platforms like Uber, Ola and Rapido for their fares, compensation practices and vehicle formats like bike-taxis. 

Green SM’s planned Bengaluru entry is part of a wider India expansion strategy. It is already operational in Delhi NCR and Hyderabad and touched the 15 Lakh rides milestone earlier this month. Green SM started India operations in June this year. 

It is now preparing to expand across six geographies, and has secured aggregator licences in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka, with plans to enter Bengaluru and Chennai.

Ride-Hailing Platforms Face Regular Roadblocks

Karnataka also plans to introduce mandatory fare meters for all taxis, including those operating through app-based aggregators, the state’s transport minister said. The transport department is preparing the necessary draft rules and legal provisions, with the government warning that vehicles found violating the prescribed fare requirements could be seized.

The proposed move follows complaints from taxi owners and drivers seeking a uniform fare structure and alleging that aggregators have been exploiting them.

The emphasis on physical meters comes as cab aggregators like Uber, Ola and Rapido face increasing scrutiny over fare structures, additional charges and booking practices.

In August, the transport department issued notices to Ola, Uber and Rapido over alleged violations of government-notified fares following complaints from driver associations that the aggregators were charging passengers fares different from those prescribed by the state government and were not paying drivers the stipulated amounts.

More recently, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) imposed penalties on Rapido and Ola over prompts asking passengers to increase their payments when drivers were not accepting the original fares.

The regulator found that messages and prompts suggesting additional payments constituted dark patterns, including confirmed shaming.

The CCPA also said it had initiated proceedings against Uber and Namma Yatri over similar practices, with investigations ongoing.

However, the proposal remains under judicial scrutiny after the Supreme Court questioned FSSAI’s proposed 365-day voluntary compliance period. FSSAI is yet to notify the final regulations, noting that it could take approximately four months to prepare and finalise the draft amendment regulations.

item.title: Fake Allahabad HC Order Row: DoT Orders Unblocking Of 95 Websites
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has directed internet service providers (ISPs) to immediately unblock 95 websites and domains that were…
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has directed internet service providers (ISPs) to immediately unblock 95 websites and domains that were earlier blocked following alleged manipulated directions from the Allahabad High Court.

The move comes amid a controversy over fraudulent court documents that were allegedly used to trigger website takedowns. In a communication to all licensees with Internet Service Authorisation, DoT asked ISPs to restore access to the listed websites with immediate effect.

The directive refers to an earlier communication dated September 2, 2026, under which ISPs were instructed to block access to the 95 websites. 

The development follows a Reuters investigation that found the government had ordered the blocking of 129 betting and gambling websites based on two purported court orders that were subsequently found to be fake.

Fake Court Orders Trigger Website Blocking Row

At the heart of the matter is the DoT’s orders to block 129 betting websites based on two purported court orders that were later found to be fake by Reuters. The publication’s report points to the flaws in the verification procedures in the country’s website-blocking framework.

Two blocking directions, which were issued on July 21 and September 2 based on orders from the Rajasthan High Court and Allahabad High Court, led to the blocking of the said websites. Neither order appeared in the courts’ online records.

The first forged order was emailed to DoT officials on July 19 in the name of advocate-on-record Aryan Chaudhary. It led to the blocking of 34 betting websites. A second purported Allahabad HC order, sent to officials on August 22 in the name of advocate Kartikey Pandey, resulted in another 95 websites being blocked.

The Allahabad HC subsequently confirmed that the August 14 order was not genuine and filed a police complaint on November 6. The Rajasthan HC registrar also reportedly said the order attributed to the court was fraudulent.

The findings prompted the Prime Minister’s Office to summon Telecom Secretary Amit Agrawal for an explanation. The telecom ministry has also initiated an internal investigation, while police are examining departmental records.

The episode follows another controversy involving purportedly fake takedown requests submitted in the name of Delhi Police against digital rights organisations Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) and Software Freedom Law Center (SFLC.in).

X told the Delhi High Court that its internal investigation found the requests to be fraudulent. The notices sought the removal of 37 posts and the withholding of accounts belonging to the two organisations and GeoBlockedIndia. The court disposed of their petitions after recording X’s statement, granting them liberty to approach it again if action was taken against their accounts.

These incidents have renewed scrutiny of government takedown requests and intermediary accountability.

Earlier, former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey alleged in July that the government directed GitHub to remove three URLs linked to his open-source messaging application bitchat.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) is reportedly considering withdrawing safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act, 2000, from social media platforms.

item.title: Jio Stops New Signups For Free Google AI Pro Subscription
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Reliance Jio has stopped accepting new claims for its free Google AI Pro subscription, which gave eligible users up to…
item.content:encoded:
Reliance Jio has stopped accepting new claims for its free Google AI Pro subscription, which gave eligible users up to 18 months of access to Google’s premium Gemini features. Users who activated the offer can continue using the subscription for up to 18 months from activation, provided they maintain an eligible recharge plan.

The redemption window ran from October 30, 2025, to October 29, 2026, according to terms and conditions listed on Jio’s website. Eligible users could activate the subscription, valued at ₹1,950 per month, through the MyJio app. Jio’s support page now says the offer is unavailable on new recharges or plan upgrades.

The offer initially covered users over the age of 18 on unlimited 5G plans priced at ₹349 or above. Starting February 11, 2026, Jio temporarily extended eligibility to users on plans priced at ₹299 or above that offered 1.5 GB of data per day. 

Subscribers were required to maintain an eligible recharge plan throughout the subscription period to retain access to the benefits. Jio reserved the right to suspend access if users failed to maintain the required plan.

Inc42 has reached out to Jio for further details on the development. The story will be updated on receiving  a response. 

The development comes a year after Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), through its AI arm Reliance Intelligence, partnered with Google to accelerate AI adoption in India by offering free Google AI Pro access to Jio users.

Announcing the partnership, RIL said the 18-month subscription would provide access to Gemini 2.5 Pro through the Gemini app, higher limits for image and video generation using Nano Banana and Veo models, expanded access to NotebookLM, and 2 TB of cloud storage, among other benefits.

The company valued the combined package at ₹35,100 per user. Eligible subscribers could activate the offer through the MyJio app.

Beyond the consumer-facing offering, the partnership also positioned Reliance Intelligence as a strategic Google Cloud partner in India, with plans to expand access to Google’s proprietary AI hardware accelerators, or TPUs, for local organisations.

Separately, Jio Platforms is in talks with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Skyroot Aerospace, and other domestic launch providers for its proposed constellation of 1,600 satellites in low Earth orbit. The company is exploring whether it can carry out the programme in India, from satellite design to launch and operations. It is also in discussions with SpaceX.

Jio Platforms listed on the BSE and NSE on October 28 at ₹1,358 apiece, a 21.4% premium to its issue price of ₹1,119.

On the financial front, the company reported a net profit of ₹8,387 Cr in Q2 FY27, marking a 13.7% increase from ₹7,379 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, net profit grew 8% from ₹7,764 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Operating revenue rose 11.4% YoY and 3.3% sequentially to ₹40,475 Cr in the quarter under review.

item.title: Raj Shamani Becomes World’s Most-Subscribed YouTube Podcaster
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Indian entrepreneur and podcaster Raj Shamani has overtaken global podcasting heavyweights Joe Rogan and Steven Bartlett to become the world’s…
item.content:encoded:
Indian entrepreneur and podcaster Raj Shamani has overtaken global podcasting heavyweights Joe Rogan and Steven Bartlett to become the world’s most-subscribed podcaster on YouTube.

His flagship show, Figuring Out With Raj Shamani, has crossed 22 Mn subscribers on the platform, surpassing Bartlett’s The Diary Of A CEO, which has 21.9 Mn subscribers, and Rogan’s The Joe Rogan Experience, which has 21.2 Mn subscribers.

Launched in 2021 from Indore, Figuring Out has witnessed rapid growth in 2026, adding 8 Mn subscribers since the beginning of the year. The show now generates approximately 1.4 Bn monthly views across platforms, while international audiences account for 22% of its YouTube subscriber base.

The podcast features conversations with prominent personalities across business, politics, science, and entertainment. Its guest list this year included French President Emmanuel Macron, neuroscientist Andrew Huberman, business professor Scott Galloway, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

Shamani has also interviewed Indian startup founders including Eternal’s Deepinder Goyal, Zerodha’s Nithin and Nikhil Kamath, CRED’s Kunal Shah, and the founders of Mamaearth, OYO, boAt, Lenskart, and Nykaa.

The podcast records 220-230 interviews a year and publishes about 150. Figuring Out Media employs more than 120 people across content, distribution, investments, and education. Shamani said he started the show to give people a way to learn from founders and other leaders regardless of where they grew up or whom they knew. 

The latest subscriber milestone comes as the entrepreneur looks to expand beyond podcasting and build a broader global media business through Figuring Out Media.

As part of its expansion plans, the company is looking to develop commercial partnerships and tap international audiences. It has also roped in global entertainment and sports agency William Morris Endeavor (WME) to support its expansion and partnered with brands such as Levi’s and ASUS.

The development comes amid growing competition among creators and media companies to build large-scale digital content businesses, with YouTube emerging as an important distribution and monetisation platform for long-form video podcasts.

Shamani is among a host of Indian podcasters growing in popularity, including BeerBiceps host Ranveer Allahabadia and Zerodha cofounder Nikhil Kamath, who hosts the ‘WTF is’ show.

item.title: Eternal Rethinks 2030 Deadline For Fully Electric Delivery Fleet
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Zomato and Blinkit parent Eternal is reconsidering its target of switching to a fully electric delivery fleet by 2030, citing…
item.content:encoded:
Zomato and Blinkit parent Eternal is reconsidering its target of switching to a fully electric delivery fleet by 2030, citing the expansion of its delivery network and uneven access to EVs.

Eternal’s chief sustainability officer Anjalli Ravi Kumar told PTI that the 2030 target “doesn’t look feasible”. She said the company remains committed to electrifying its fleet and is working on a new timeline based on vehicle availability, government policies, and the transport needs of its businesses.

Zomato had around 1.5 Lakh monthly active delivery partners when it set the original target. Eternal now has around 12 Lakh riders across its food delivery and quick commerce platforms. Kumar said the company needs to onboard about 30 Lakh riders a year to sustain this base, raising the question of whether riders can reliably access EVs across 900 cities.

Responding to a question on Eternal committing to a 2035 deadline, Kumar said the company is still working on a date and its decision would partly depend on how widely EV policies are rolled out across the country.

She added that the revised target would cover transport across the group, including the trucks and smaller commercial vehicles that Hyperpure uses for deliveries.

Delivery Platforms’ EV Plans 

Eternal’s reassessment comes amid a broader push by food delivery and quick commerce platforms to electrify their delivery fleets.

In March 2025, rival Swiggy announced its target of transitioning to a 100% EV delivery fleet by 2030. The company began piloting EVs in 2021 through a partnership with Reliance BP Mobility and later launched Swiggy XL EV, which uses electric three-wheelers for bulk orders

Zomato began piloting EV bike rentals for delivery partners in Delhi NCR in June 2025, with plans to expand the initiative based on uptake. As of March 2025, it had over 37,000 active food delivery partners using EVs.

Eternal has also introduced measures such as equal payouts for EV and petrol-powered vehicle users, rental options through its delivery partner app and the EV Bazaar to familiarise riders with available electric vehicle models.

The EV transition is also extending to larger commercial vehicles. Last month, Amazon partnered with Tata Motors to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across its transportation network in India, signalling the growing adoption of electric vehicles in goods movement and logistics.

States are also weighing requirements for delivery platforms. In August 2026, Maharashtra proposed extending its bike-taxi rules to food delivery, quick commerce, and ecommerce platforms, including Swiggy, Zomato, and Zepto. The proposed rules include an EV mandate, a 2% rider welfare levy, GPS tracking, and insurance cover.

item.title: Smartphone Price Hike: Samsung, Xiaomi Models Get Costlier By Up To ₹4,000 In India
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Samsung and Xiaomi have increased smartphone prices by up to ₹4,000 across 48 variants in India amid rising memory chip…
item.content:encoded:
Samsung and Xiaomi have increased smartphone prices by up to ₹4,000 across 48 variants in India amid rising memory chip prices and subdued consumer demand.

Prices for about 30 Samsung phones as well as 19 Xiaomi phones have been increased in a range of ₹1,000-4,000 between November 15-16.

Samsung’s latest revision covers 14 variants across its Galaxy A07 5G, A17 5G, A36, A37, A56, A57 and F17 5G lineups, with most models becoming costlier by ₹2,000. 

The Galaxy A57 saw the steepest hike of ₹4,000, taking the 8GB+256GB and 12GB+256GB variants to ₹66,999 and ₹76,499, respectively. Its November 15 revision also raised prices of seven Galaxy M17 5G, M17e and F70e 5G variants by ₹2,000 each.

Xiaomi, meanwhile, revised prices across 19 Redmi variants. Hikes ranged from ₹1,000 to ₹4,000, with the Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G seeing the steepest increase. Its 8GB+128GB and 8GB+256GB variants now cost ₹40,999 and ₹43,999, respectively.

This adds to an ongoing trend in the smartphone market where higher average selling prices have led to a weaker consumer demand. Damp demand during the recently concluded Diwali sales, one of the major occasions for such purchases in India, is evidence to that.  

Smartphone sales volumes dipped as much as 20% year-on-year (YoY) during the four-day festive period between November 6-9, as per data from All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA).

While overall sales value remained broadly in line with the previous year due to higher average selling prices, the contraction in volumes squeezed retailer margins and store profitability.

AIMRA also reported that offline smartphone sales volumes fell nearly 40% in the seven days preceding Dhanteras (November 6), as consumers delayed purchases in anticipation of festive offers. Financing constraints further affected demand, with only 60-70% of logged loan applications receiving approval during the festive period.

Against this backdrop, the latest price increases could add to the affordability concerns, particularly in the price-sensitive budget and mid-range segments.

AI Data Centre Demand Adds To Memory Chip Supply Constraints

The price revisions come amid a broader surge in memory chip prices at the behest of sharper demand from AI infrastructure and data centres.

AI infra particularly relies on DRAM, which provides the high-speed memory GPUs needed to process AI workloads, and NAND flash, which enables cost-efficient storage of the massive datasets that enable AI model training. These chips are also essential components in smartphones, laptops, gaming consoles and other consumer electronics. 

Thus, the rise in AI development globally is now creating tightened supply chains for manufacturers and pushing up procurement costs. The impact extends across consumer electronics, with smartphone, PC and gaming console makers facing higher component costs.

This was also highlighted by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who recently flagged the growing competition for memory resources during a podcast. He argued that while large amounts of DRAM in personal computers often remain underutilised and could be put to better use in cloud infrastructure. He also pointed to supply constraints in the memory market and said its usual price correction mechanism was not working effectively.

Meanwhile, expanding semiconductor manufacturing capacity remains challenging, as setting up new facilities requires significant investment and time.

item.title: Oister Global Launches ₹600 Cr Growth-Stage Focused Deeptech Fund
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Private markets asset manager Oister Global has launched a growth-stage deeptech fund with a target corpus of ₹600 Cr. The…
item.content:encoded:
Private markets asset manager Oister Global has launched a growth-stage deeptech fund with a target corpus of ₹600 Cr. The firm will target backing Indian startups developing technologies across strategic sectors.

The Oister Deep Tech Fund, registered as a SEBI Category II AIF, intends to raise ₹400 Cr, along with a ₹200 Cr greenshoe option to build a concentrated portfolio of 8-10 companies.

In a statement, the investment firm shared that it will focus on mature deeptech companies that have developed commercially viable technologies and are looking to scale their operations. Its investment focus will span sectors like spacetech, defence and aerospace, semiconductors and electronics, quantum technologies, advanced mobility, advanced materials and energy storage.

The fund will target companies with proprietary intellectual property (IP), including patents in India and international markets, multiple revenue streams and customers across domestic and global markets. 

“Early-stage investors back the idea, and larger institutions tend to wait until a company is well past its hardest years. The growth stage in between, where technology turns into a business, has had very few committed investors. That is the gap we saw, and it is why we launched the Oister Deep Tech Fund,” said Rohit Bhayana, cofounder and co-CEO of Oister Global.

Bridging The Growth-Stage Funding Gap

The fund launch comes amid a growing investor interest in India’s budding deeptech ecosystem.

Recent examples include AUM Ventures’ ₹750 Cr India Innovation Fund II, Speciale Invest’s proposed ₹1,400 Cr growth-stage fund and Celesta Capital’s planned ₹2,000 Cr India-focused deeptech fund. Meanwhile, Yali Capital closed its maiden deeptech fund at ₹893 Cr in July 2025.

As a result, the overall investment numbers have also been on the up. Indian deeptech startups raised nearly $365 Mn across 66 deals in H1 2026, representing a 17% YoY growth in funding, compared with $310 Mn in H1 2025, according to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report: H1 2026. 

Pertinent to note that much of this capital deployment has continued to remain concentrated in the early stage, with not many investors showing the same enthusiasm when it comes to startups operating in the latter stages. 

Citing this discrepancy, Oister Global said that growth-stage funding can help bridge the gap by providing patient capital to companies that have already de-risked their technology but require larger investments to manufacture products, fulfil orders and expand into international markets.

The fund has already identified an initial shortlist of companies across its target sectors, with further investments to be evaluated as capital is deployed.

Oister previously backed startups in the country through its growth-stage and secondary investment vehicles. Its portfolio includes companies such as BlackBuck, Servify, M1xchange, Kuku FM and Purplle, among others.

In May, it launched its third ACE fund with a ₹500 Cr corpus after the second ACE fund closed with a ₹400 Cr corpus, twice its initial target of ₹200 Cr. The third fund took its total secondaries allotment to ₹1,000 Cr.

Besides directly investing in startups, Oister also operates with a fund of funds thesis. Till date, it has turned limited partner for various startup funds for VC firms including Blume Ventures, Speciale Invest and Stride Ventures.

item.title: upGrad Enters Enterprise Advisory With Launch Of upGrad Next
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Edtech unicorn upGrad has launched upGrad Next, an enterprise advisory practice that will help companies restructure their organisations and prepare…
item.content:encoded:
Edtech unicorn upGrad has launched upGrad Next, an enterprise advisory practice that will help companies restructure their organisations and prepare their employees for AI adoption.

The new vertical will advise senior executives on organisational structure, hiring, employee compensation, and workforce development. upGrad’s existing enterprise business, which the company said worked with more than 700 organisations in FY26, will help put these recommendations into practice through employee reskilling, leadership development, and hiring.

The new vertical will be led by four managing directors – former Deloitte partners Anandorup Ghose and Krishna Chaitanya Malladi, former EY partner Hrishikesh Godbole and former Deloitte executive Dinkar Pawan. They will advise companies on organisational restructuring and workforce transformation, with more senior leaders expected to join in the coming weeks.

The launch comes as businesses adopt AI and look to restructure their operations and workforce. While companies have invested in digital transformation over the past decade, preparing employees for AI-led changes remains a challenge.

In a LinkedIn post announcing the launch, upGrad cofounder and chairperson Ronnie Screwvala said the next decade would focus on reshaping workforces to help companies manage and realise returns from their digital transformation investments.

Screwvala said companies would need advice on how to organise their teams, hire, pay, and train employees, along with help implementing these changes. He added that upGrad Next would move away from the traditional consulting model, where fees depend on the number of consultants deployed and their billing rates.

“Not a myriad of consultants, not the traditional headcount-times-billing-rate model, but real, strong experience, sharpened with the power of AI and accountable for outcomes,” Screwvala said.


upGrad’s Unacademy Buyout

The launch comes two months after upGrad closed its acquisition of rival edtech platform Unacademy in September 2026 in a deal valued at just over $200 Mn. The transaction followed months of negotiations and regulatory clearances.

Unacademy cofounder Gaurav Munjal announced the deal’s closure and acknowledged that the startup had sold for a fraction of its peak valuation of $3.5 Bn in 2021.

Following the acquisition, Munjal announced his decision to step down as Unacademy’s CEO and transition to the role of executive chairman.

On the financial front, upGrad reported a 52% decline in net loss to ₹130 Cr in FY26 from ₹274 Cr in FY25, while gross revenue rose 7% to ₹2,070 Cr. The company attributed the improvement to AI-led efficiencies, which helped lower its marketing and technology costs even as revenue increased.

item.title: Jio In Talks With ISRO, Skyroot For 1,600-Satellite Constellation: Report
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Jio Platforms has begun talks with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Skyroot Aerospace, and other Indian launch providers to…
item.content:encoded:
Jio Platforms has begun talks with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Skyroot Aerospace, and other Indian launch providers to deploy satellites for its proposed 1,600-satellite low Earth orbit (LEO) constellation.

The company wants to explore domestic launch options first and is also considering SpaceX, Mint reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Jio is evaluating whether it can carry out the entire programme from satellite design, engineering, integration, and testing to launch, deployment, and operations in India.

Inc42 has reached out to Jio and Skyroot for comment. The story will be updated on receiving a response.

Jio’s Satellite Rollout

Jio is targeting a September 2027 test launch involving a handful of satellites to evaluate the network’s hardware, software, and other technologies. It plans to begin mass deployment in early 2028, put around 400-450 satellites into orbit by 2030, and complete the constellation by 2035.

The company plans to launch an initial batch of about 390 satellites in phases and establish 23 ground stations across India. It is in talks with multiple operators to line up launches over the next two years, according to Mint.

Reliance Industries outlined plans for an Indian-owned LEO constellation at its 49th annual general meeting in June. Jio Platforms MD Akash Ambani said the company was evaluating whether to develop its own constellation while exploring partnerships with global satellite operators.

Leasing capacity from these operators could help Jio offer services sooner. The company also plans to build ground stations that can support both partner networks and its own satellites.

Jio will compete with SpaceX’s Starlink and Eutelsat OneWeb, which is backed by Bharti Group, in India’s satellite broadband market. Amazon Leo is also seeking to enter the market.

In October, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk alleged that Indian business interests were obstructing Starlink’s entry. Reliance said it welcomed competition from Starlink and that Jio’s own satellite services were still awaiting government clearances. 

India has handled large satellite deployments before. ISRO’s heavy-lift LVM3 rocket put 72 OneWeb satellites into orbit across two missions in 2022 and 2023. Skyroot Aerospace and Agnikul Cosmos have flown privately developed rockets, while startups such as EtherealX are developing their own launch vehicles.

item.title: [Update] SBI Data Breach: FIR Filed Over Alleged Theft Of 3.75 Lakh Bank Records
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Update | November 16, 12:30 IST Police in CBD-Belapur registered an FIR on November 12 over the alleged theft of…
item.content:encoded:
Update | November 16, 12:30 IST

Police in CBD-Belapur registered an FIR on November 12 over the alleged theft of about 3.75 Lakh bank records from a server at State Bank of India’s (SBI) global IT Centre. 

The FIR came about a month after the alleged breach, The Times of India reported.

According to the complaint cited in the report, unidentified individuals allegedly operating under the name Siriusim accessed the server between October 10 and 15. They allegedly took about 32 CSV files containing 3.75 Lakh records from SBI applications, along with JSON files and 2,721 PDFs containing personal information.

The files included loan application records, account-opening forms, customer contact details, and addresses.

The complaint said some of the stolen data was later posted on the dark web. SBI had earlier said its preliminary review identified 3,897 records containing customers’ personal information among the 3.75 Lakh records found there.

Police said SBI launched an internal inquiry after its officials spotted the data on the dark web. The bank told police it had removed the data from the platform and that the information had not been misused.

Police have registered the FIR against unidentified persons, invoking provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to theft and criminal conspiracy, along with sections of the Information Technology Act. The investigation is underway to trace those responsible.

Original| October 21, 11:32 IST

State Bank of India (SBI) has flagged the exposure of 3,897 customer records containing personal information on the dark web, including mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, and residential addresses.

The public sector lender, in an exchange filing, said its preliminary analysis of around 3.75 Lakh records available on the dark web identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information.

The data also included branch details, customer information file identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan and lead records, according to the bank.

SBI said it received alerts about the suspected exposure on October 16 from its threat intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency, and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In).

The disclosure follows claims attributed to a threat actor using the name Siriusim, which cybersecurity account CyberPulse56 shared on X. The actor claimed to possess around 3.75 Lakh rows of SBI-linked data and 2,722 PDF documents, including loan applications, supporting documents, and account-opening forms. Inc42 could not independently verify these claims.

The number of records examined does not establish that 3.75 Lakh customers were affected, with SBI’s preliminary findings identifying 3,897 customer records containing personal information.

SBI Launches Probe Into Data Exposure

SBI said it had activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and engaged an independent CERT-In-empanelled cybersecurity agency to investigate.

The investigation will seek to establish the authenticity and completeness of the data, identify the source and extent of the exposure, and assess potential risks to customers and the bank.

The lender said its core banking and business functions continued to operate normally, with no material impact on operations, financial performance, or business continuity. It added that remedial and preventive measures were being implemented while the assessment continued.

The incident comes amid growing concerns over AI-driven cybercrime and digital fraud. State-run Punjab National Bank (PNB) has also warned customers about threats such as AI-generated voice clones, deepfakes and phishing attacks.

The SBI incident follows other customer data breaches at Indian financial services companies. In February last year, Angel One disclosed unauthorised access to some of its Amazon Web Services resources after receiving alerts from its dark-web monitoring partner.

Prior to that, personal data belonging to over 3 Cr Star Health customers surfaced for sale online, including names, addresses, PAN details, and medical histories. The insurer reported the breach to CERT-In and the insurance regulator, initiated a forensic investigation, and moved court to restrict access to the leaked information.

item.title: AI Startups To Watch: 5 Startups That Caught Our Eye In November
item.dc:creator: Ankush Das
item.description: AI in India has moved past the phase of picking a single large language model. For two years, the loudest…
item.content:encoded:
AI in India has moved past the phase of picking a single large language model. For two years, the loudest question in boardrooms was which model an enterprise would standardise on. While that question has largely settled, the challenge has shifted to running these models efficiently, reliably and at scale.

The issue is especially pronounced at the enterprise scale, where multiple AI models are employed. A model powerful enough to handle complex reasoning may be too expensive for routine queries, while a smaller, cheaper model may struggle with sophisticated workloads.

This leaves enterprises grappling with a fundamental trade-off: how to deliver the intelligence their applications need without compromising on speed, performance or cost.

Therefore, the near-term prize for Indian builders looks less like a fresh frontier model and more like the enormous market for serving existing ones cheaply and reliably. 

Investor capital is following the same logic. 

In late October, enterprise AI startup AuxoAI raised $20.7 Mn, and Blacksmith netted $66 Mn at a unicorn valuation. Both startups backed the same thesis of putting AI to work inside businesses. Meanwhile, QwikBuild picked up $2.3 Mn for its enterprise AI platform, and Spill Games raised $10.5 Mn for AI-led mobile gaming. 

The pattern shows that investors are betting less on the next frontier model and more on the companies that deploy the ones that exist.

Against this backdrop, Inc42 returns with its monthly series, Five AI Startups To Watch. The 14th edition highlights five emerging startups building across inference routing, semantic video intelligence, autonomous commerce, AI-native CRM and pipeline generation.

These are not simply startups using AI as a feature, but building businesses around the infrastructure, autonomy, and measurement that make an AI system worth deploying.

With that said, here are the five emerging AI startups that made it to the November edition of Inc42’s AI Startups To Watch.

Editor’s Note: This is not a ranking. The startups featured here are a curated selection by the Inc42 editorial team and are listed alphabetically.

BLUE | Turning CCTV Into Intelligence Layer

Most CCTV feeds an enterprise runs are never looked at until after something has gone wrong, and even then, the search means sifting through months of data. Storing it is expensive, analysing it costs more, and the AI that could help sits out of reach for most sites.

BLUE is building an AI-native video data lake that turns CCTV cameras into a searchable layer. Founded in 2023, the Bengaluru startup is led by CEO Kunal Kislay, with Ashish Mehta, Mohit Garg and Nishant Sinha, and harnesses a codec that compresses meaning at capture rather than scanning raw pixels downstream.

Its codec cuts storage by up to 90% and compute at the source by up to eight times, encoding objects, events and behaviours as structured data. Teams can ask their cameras questions in plain English, with agents tuned for retail, warehousing, oil and gas and manufacturing. BLUE runs in the cloud, on-premises, or in a hybrid environment.

BLUE counts Britannia and Hindustan Petroleum among its customers in the global video analytics market, projected to reach $33.61 Bn by 2031.


Kily | Autonomous Agents For Marketplace Growth

A consumer brand selling online now has to manage listings, pricing and ads across a growing list of marketplaces, from Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra to Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart. A brand with a few hundred SKUs can face thousands of campaigns and price checks that no human team can keep up with.

Kily is an autonomous agent that takes over those operations, configuring, monitoring and optimising itself rather than recommending actions for people to approve. The Bengaluru startup was founded in March 2025 by ex-Flipkart executives Sankalp Mehrotra and Anurag Singh, alongside ex-Amazon Ads executive Sharad Chitlangia.

Its Core Decision AI coordinates specialist agents set bids and budgets, watch price parity and flag stock-out risks, all to drive profitable growth. Kily positions itself as a P&L management layer for ecommerce, deciding and executing rather than merely suggesting.

Kily claims to work with over 50 brands, including ITC, Unilever, Mondelez and Coca-Cola in India’s retail ecommerce market.

Revspot | An AI-Native Revenue Infrastructure For High-Ticket B2C Businesses

For businesses selling high-value products and services in sectors such as real estate, education and wealth management, potential customers often slip through the cracks at different stages of the sales process. Outdated customer data, delayed follow-ups, and time spent chasing leads with little intent to purchase collectively hurt conversions. 

Revspot is building an AI growth agent called Spot that generates qualified pipeline end to end. The Bengaluru startup was founded in 2024 by Darshan Subash, Chirag Wadhera and Varun Garg.

Spot decides who to target, what to say and where to reach them, then launches campaigns, enriches every lead, runs voice agents to qualify intent and follows up over WhatsApp before handing the team only the buyers worth meeting. Nothing goes live until a human approves the plan.

The startup says it serves more than 50 customers across real estate, education, automotive and wealth management, and raised $4.8 Mn in a Series A co-led by Inflexor Ventures and Info Edge Ventures, with Pentathlon Ventures, Silicon Road Ventures and Titan Capital. It operates in the global AI sales agent market, estimated at $3.4 Bn in 2026 and projected to reach $15.8 Bn by 2033.

RouterPlus | The Single Key for Smart LLM Routing

Teams that build on large language models now juggle several providers, API keys and contracts, and often pick a model on global benchmarks that have little to do with their own workload. The result is cost, latency and quality they cannot really control, and bills that rise as usage grows.

RouterPlus is an LLM routing and inference layer behind a single key. Founded in 2026 by Alok Bishoyi and Lakshmi Narayana, the startup routes each request based on a customer’s own evals and production traffic rather than global leaderboards. Its catalogue spans closed and open-weight models, from Claude, GPT and Gemini to Qwen and DeepSeek, with the goal of matching the right model to each task.

The gateway also offers reserved capacity through providers such as Modal, Fireworks and Baseten, stores no prompts, supports regional routing and bring-your-own-key, and helps teams shift from closed to open-source models as they upgrade their systems.

RouterPlus operates in the AI model router market, estimated at $100 Mn in 2025 and projected to reach $4.1 Bn by 2035.

 

Superleap | The AI-Native CRM For Revenue Teams

For years, customer relationship management (CRM) systems have served more as reporting tools than as platforms that help sales teams close deals. Sales representatives are expected to feed them with data but rarely see any direct benefit. As a result, they often skip updates, leaving these systems with incomplete, outdated and increasingly unreliable information.

Superleap is rebuilding the category as an AI-native revenue operating system. The Bengaluru startup was founded in 2024 by former Unacademy operators Subham Kumar Boundia, Alok Maurya and Saurabh Maheshwari.

Under the hood sit SuperOS, a unified data layer; SuperSense, a customer-intelligence layer; and SuperAgents, an agentic layer that automates tasks across the revenue cycle, alongside AI voice bots and MCP integrations with tools such as WhatsApp, Slack and ChatGPT. Its Superleap Deploy team promises migration off legacy CRMs in under two months with zero disruption.

Superleap counts Razorpay, Aakash Education, Cars24 and MediBuddy as its customers in the global CRM market, projected to reach about $321 Bn by 2034 at a CAGR of 12.4%.

Update | November 16, 2026

Urban Company shareholders have approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr through the issuance of securities. The approval clears the way for the company’s proposed QIP.

Shareholders approved the special resolution by postal ballot yesterday. According to the company’s exchange filing, 99.29% of votes were cast in favour and 0.71% against.

Original | October 13, 2026

Urban Company’s board today approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr, alongside approving its financial performance for the September quarter. The proposed funding could involve issuance of equity shares, warrants, fully convertible debentures and convertible preference shares. 

The fundraise will be executed in one or more tranches via preferential allotment, private placement or one or more qualified institutional placements (QIPs), subject to shareholder approval. The final issue pricing and structure is yet to be determined. 

“The business is materially larger than at listing, growth has stepped up, and we now operate three businesses at scale with proven economics. The proposed raise of up to ₹2,500 Cr is about flexibility: it lets us invest with conviction across each of them, cement leadership in InstaHelp, and pursue inorganic opportunities selectively, without trading off one for another,” Urban Company said in a letter to shareholders. 

The fundraise proposal comes at a time when Urban Company’s quick home services vertical InstaHelp is facing tough competition from the likes of Snabbit and Pronto, resulting in the prospect of a war for market share fuelled by cash burn. 

Hefty investments in powering the quick home services vertical is also creating a dent in Urban Company’s bottom line. For the September quarter, Urban Company’s net loss more than tripled YoY to ₹182.5 Cr, while operating revenue jumped 41% YoY to ₹537.29 Cr.

Separately, the board also granted in-principle approval to explore residential air conditioners as a new business category under its product brand Native. This would be subject to further evaluations and final board clearances. 

“This category represents a large market in which the Company already services millions of units annually, providing it with first-hand insights into the existing product gaps and customer needs,” noted UC’s board. 

Urban Company made its debut on the bourses just around one year ago. Hence, its proposed fundraise puts it among the ranks of several new-age tech companies like Kissht, Swiggy, Ather Energy, and Ola Electric that have sought to return to the public markets for fresh capital soon after their IPOs. 

On a quarterly basis, its net loss nearly doubled from ₹92.1 Cr. Operating revenue remained nearly flat compared with ₹528.3 Cr in Q1 FY27. 

The company’s adjusted EBITDA loss for the quarter widened to ₹144 Cr, due to a “deliberate” ₹174 Cr investment in InstaHelp. The company also gave a timeline to improve its bottom line performance in the near future.

“We remain on track for Adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and Adjusted EBITDA of ₹1,000 Cr by FY31,” it said.
